---
title: Receive vendor webhooks
description: Give a vendor an address on your instance to post webhooks to, then check each delivery came from the vendor, act on it and mark it handled.
---

Many vendors post a webhook when something changes. With an endpoint on your instance, a connector can act on that change at once instead of waiting for its next scheduled read. Marfa stores each delivery exactly as it arrived and answers the vendor; everything after that is the connector's job.

A connector built on [the connector kit](/build/connector) needs only the endpoint and [an `inbound` section](#with-the-kit). The rest of this guide covers the operations underneath, for a connector built directly on the API.

The examples follow a recipe box connector with a key of its own. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a [TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk) client made with that key, and `connectorId` is the registration's ID.

## Create an endpoint

[Create an inbound endpoint](/api-reference/inbound-webhooks/createInboundEndpoint) makes a private address on your instance for the vendor to post to. You usually do this once, by hand:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa connectors endpoints create 01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99 \
  --label "recipe box webhooks" --duplicate-header X-Delivery-Id
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /connectors/01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99/endpoints
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "label": "recipe box webhooks", "duplicate_header": "X-Delivery-Id" }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.POST("/connectors/{id}/endpoints", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: { label: "recipe box webhooks", duplicate_header: "X-Delivery-Id" },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="201"
{
  "id": "01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe",
  "connector_id": "01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99",
  "label": "recipe box webhooks",
  "duplicate_header": "x-delivery-id",
  "path": "/inbound/PLPN1aDOk55XjNqHkHKfSD-8a9SoehUsbTvSU_dhEGM",
  "created_at": "2026-11-19T00:27:05.540Z",
  "retired_at": null
}
```

- **Save the `path` now.** The vendor posts without a credential, so the address itself is the secret. Only this answer shows it in full: every later read shows `/inbound/****` and its last four characters.
- **Give the vendor the address:** your instance's public [address](/run/address) followed by the `path`. The CLI adds the whole address as `url`.
- **Keep the vendor's signing secret in the connector's settings.** Marfa never holds it.
- **`duplicate_header`** names the header whose value identifies a delivery, such as `X-GitHub-Delivery` for GitHub, so Marfa can point out a delivery the vendor sends twice.

## Read the deliveries

[List inbound deliveries](/api-reference/inbound-webhooks/listInboundDeliveries) answers the deliveries not yet handled, oldest first, without their bodies. `state=handled` or `state=any` reads the others, and `endpoint_id` limits the list to one endpoint:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
GET /connectors/01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99/deliveries
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: page } = await marfa.GET("/connectors/{id}/deliveries", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
});
```

Each delivery is the request as it arrived:

```json title="A delivery"
{
  "id": "01a1f133-2e4a-7567-a309-bb4fb58ba295",
  "endpoint_id": "01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe",
  "received_at": "2026-11-19T00:27:05.674Z",
  "method": "POST",
  "query": "",
  "headers": [
    ["content-type", "application/json"],
    ["x-delivery-id", "d-100"],
    ["x-signature", "sha256=3dca2ba66de6139cbc7adca0d6a04a735ccf40ffdb37296ca389fe6c811e6c54"]
  ],
  "size": 18,
  "sha256": "fdb8cba1273830698d1a719dd7abc36031b21747e148d8620fe99ddabe3cd125",
  "duplicate_of": { "id": "01a1f133-2e26-7330-bebc-856e33e8b215", "outcome": "processed" },
  "handled_at": null,
  "outcome": null
}
```

- **Headers keep every value, with names in lower case.** A header sent twice appears twice, in the order it came. Headers whose names begin with `Tailscale-` aren't stored, since they name who on your tailnet sent the request.
- **Read until `next_cursor` is `null`.** A page holds 50 by default, and `limit` takes up to 200.
- **Only the connector's own key** reads deliveries. Any other key is refused `403 forbidden`, the owner's included.

## Check the signature

Anyone who learns the address can post to it, so a stored delivery **proves nothing about who sent it**. Most vendors sign the body with the secret they share with you, and send the signature in a header. [Get an inbound delivery's body](/api-reference/inbound-webhooks/getInboundDeliveryBody) answers the body byte for byte, as `application/octet-stream`:

```ts title="src/check.ts"
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

const { data: body } = await marfa.GET("/connectors/{id}/deliveries/{delivery_id}/body", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId, delivery_id: delivery.id } },
  parseAs: "arrayBuffer",
});
const signature = delivery.headers.find(([name]) => name === "x-signature")?.[1] ?? "";
const expected = `sha256=${createHmac("sha256", secret).update(new Uint8Array(body!)).digest("hex")}`;
const genuine =
  signature.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(signature), Buffer.from(expected));
```

Each vendor names its own header, prefix and encoding, so follow its documentation. Compare in constant time, as `timingSafeEqual` does, and **always over the bytes as they arrived**: parsing the body first changes them. A delivery that fails the check isn't the vendor's, so read nothing from it and mark it `rejected`.

## Act on a delivery

Treat a delivery as **a prompt to read the vendor**, not as the vendor's state. Vendors send webhooks out of order, twice, or not at all.

Take from the delivery only what names the thing that changed, such as a recipe's ID, then fetch it from the vendor and write it as [Pull from a vendor](/build/connector-pull) shows. **Keep the scheduled read as well**, for the webhook that never comes.

When a delivery repeats the `duplicate_header` value of an earlier one on the same endpoint, Marfa stores both and fills the later one's `duplicate_of` with the earliest one it still holds. If that one's `outcome` is `processed`, you've already acted on the change.

## Mark it handled

[Mark inbound deliveries handled](/api-reference/inbound-webhooks/markInboundDeliveriesHandled) takes 1 to 200 IDs and one outcome:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /connectors/01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99/deliveries/handled
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "ids": ["01a1f133-2e26-7330-bebc-856e33e8b215"], "outcome": "processed" }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/connectors/{id}/deliveries/handled", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: { ids: ["01a1f133-2e26-7330-bebc-856e33e8b215"], outcome: "processed" },
});
```

- **`processed`:** you read the vendor because of the delivery, and the run succeeded.
- **`duplicate`:** an earlier delivery of the same change was processed.
- **`rejected`:** the delivery failed your check, or names nothing you act on.

**The first mark stands**: marking a delivery again leaves the mark it has. So mark a delivery `processed` only after the run that used it ends without error. A delivery you leave unmarked comes back in the next listing, and a run that fails loses nothing.

## What the vendor is told

Marfa answers the vendor **before your connector sees anything**, and many vendors send a request again when it's refused:

| Answer | When |
| --- | --- |
| `202`, with the delivery's `id` | Marfa stored the delivery. |
| `404 not_found` | The address isn't a live endpoint: it was retired, never existed, or its connector was deleted or its key revoked or expired. |
| `413 request_too_large` | The body is over 25 MiB, unless the owner set another `inbound_max_bytes`. |
| `408 request_timeout` | No byte of the body arrived for 30 seconds. |
| `429 rate_limited`, with `Retry-After` | The endpoint is past its request limit, 600 a window unless the owner set another. |
| `503 inbound_unavailable`, with `Retry-After` | The connector's unhandled deliveries fill its backlog. |

Marfa stores nothing for a refused request. Marking a delivery handled frees its place in the backlog, but **only age removes it**: a handled delivery after 7 days and an unhandled one after 30, unless the owner [sets other windows](/run/settings#change-settings-while-it-runs). [Errors](/api-reference/errors) lists every refusal.

## Replace an endpoint

To move a vendor to a new address, create a new endpoint, give the vendor its path, and **retire the old one** once the vendor has switched. A registration holds at most 10 live endpoints, and an eleventh is refused `409 conflict`.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa connectors endpoints retire 01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99 01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe
```

```http tab="HTTP"
DELETE /connectors/01a1f12f-798c-70d4-b57b-d57feabdad99/endpoints/01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.DELETE("/connectors/{id}/endpoints/{endpoint_id}", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId, endpoint_id: "01a1f133-2dc4-75cf-84fd-eb21a8a270fe" } },
});
```

[Retiring an endpoint](/api-reference/inbound-webhooks/retireInboundEndpoint) keeps it in the list with `retired_at` set, and its address answers `404`. Its deliveries stay readable and **still count toward the backlog**, so read and mark them as usual.

## With the kit

A connector built on the kit adds an `inbound` section, and the kit reads the deliveries, checks them and marks them:

```ts title="src/main.ts"
inbound: {
  verify: (delivery, env) =>
    verifyHmac({
      secret: env.RECIPES_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      body: delivery.body,
      signature: delivery.header("X-Signature"),
      prefix: "sha256=",
    }),
  hints: () => "everything",
},
```

- **`verify`** says whether a delivery came from the vendor, here with the kit's `verifyHmac`. Declare the secret in `env` as a `secret`.
- **`hints`** says what the delivery tells the connector changed. `"everything"` makes the next run read the vendor whole.

Each run collects up to 500 deliveries, and a connector the kit runs on a schedule also looks for new ones between runs. The run's report counts the deliveries it processed, rejected and found duplicate. The template's README, `template/README.md` in marfa-connectors, describes `inbound` in full.

The rules behind this page are in the [inbound webhooks](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/inbound-webhooks.md) chapter of the contract.
